title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 149-152). X is a smooth variety or orbifold/stack; Grothendieck's target is the stable compactification of M_{g,ν}. Θ is a divisor with normal crossings that need not be strict (self-crossings allowed). Θ^{(d)} is the stratum of codimension ≥ d. D_d is the normalisation of Θ^{(d)}, parametrising points together with d local branches. D_{d,d'} (d > d') are the flag varieties: a codim-d point with a chosen sub-d'-tuple of its branches. These come with maps D_{d,d'} → D_d and D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}.

The objects:
- X^{*∞} = V*_{Θ,X} is the 'structure à l'infini': the deleted tubular (pro-)neighbourhood of Θ in X* = X∖Θ.
- Π̃_d is the fundamental groupoid of the deleted neighbourhood V*_{Θ_d,D_d} attached to the codim-d stratum. It is an extension of Π_1 of the open stratum by the local torus Z^d of meridian loops; for M_{g,ν} these are multi-Dehn twists.
- Π̃_{2,1} is the analogous groupoid for D_{2,1}. It maps to Π̃_1 (forget the second branch) and to Π̃_2 (forget the choice of branch).

Corollary 2 (formula 246): Π_1(X^{*∞}) ≃ 2-colim(Π̃_1 ← Π̃_{2,1} → Π̃_2). This is a pushout of groupoids, so only codimension 1 and 2 matter.

Proof sketch: a local Van Kampen analysis shows that, up to 2-equivalence, Θ^{(3)} can be neglected, i.e. X may be replaced by X∖Θ^{(3)}. Two points support this:
- The deleted neighbourhood U∖Θ is literally the same set for X and X∖Θ^{(3)}. Only the cofinal system of neighbourhoods changes near Θ^{(3)}.
- Θ^{(3)} has real codimension 6, so π_0 and π_1 are unaffected.
Once Θ^{(3)} is removed, the boundary is covered by the pieces over the open codim-1 and codim-2 strata, glued along the flag piece D_{2,1}. Ordinary groupoid Van Kampen then gives the pushout.

The marginal note asks to make explicit how the higher Π̃_i (i ≥ 3) sit in this colimit. For example, Π̃_3 should itself be the colimit of the diagram Π̃_{3,2,1} → Π̃_{3,2}, Π̃_{3,1}, …, a compatibility of the stratified (flag) system with the colimit.

Corollary 3 (formula 247): suppose X^{*∞} → X* is a 1-equivalence (equivalence on Π_1). Then Π_1 of the open variety is the same pushout. For M_{g,ν} this hypothesis holds in the stable range: the Harvey boundary is homotopy equivalent to the curve complex, which Harer showed to be simply connected in that range. The conclusion is then that the Teichmüller modular group Γ_{g,ν} is the amalgam of the groupoids at infinity attached to one curve and to two disjoint curves, along the flag 'pair with a marked curve'.

This is the local, purely topological engine behind the 'two-level' reconstruction principle of the Esquisse: the tower is determined by modular dimension ≤ 2. A 'Corollaire 4' (sub-systems of strata, open-closed parts D'_i of D_i) is begun and crossed out. The next page replaces it by Θ-admissible closed subsets Σ, a generalisation of these colimit formulas to unions of boundary components.
errors: Formula (247) writes Π_1 X. Under the stated hypothesis it must mean Π_1 X* = Π_1(X∖Θ), the open part (e.g. M_{g,ν} itself). Π_1 of the compactification X is the quotient by the meridians.

The 1-equivalence hypothesis and the colimit implicitly need connectedness/π_0 compatibility and an orbifold/stack treatment (D_d with automorphism groups, Π̃ as groupoids of stacks). These are not addressed on this page.

The 'local analysis' justifying neglect of Θ^{(3)} is only sketched. The subtlety is that neighbourhoods of Θ∖Θ^{(3)} in X∖Θ^{(3)} can be thinner near Θ^{(3)} than U∖Θ^{(3)}. The conclusion (π_0, π_1 unchanged, real codim 6) is nevertheless correct.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of the deleted neighbourhood of a normal-crossings boundary as a 2-pushout of the groupoids at infinity of the codim-1 stratum, the codim-2 stratum and the (2,1)-flag stratum; codim ≥ 3 strata negligible
ideas.modern_name: Van Kampen for the boundary of a toroidal/NC compactification; complex-of-groups description of π1 of the boundary (Harvey bordification / curve complex quotient)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Boggi (π1 of boundary neighbourhoods of M̄_{g,n}); Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (Teichmüller tower); general complexes of groups (Haefliger, Brown)
ideas.where_published: Spirit announced in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower determined by modular dimension ≤ 2); this explicit pushout formula is not known to me in published form

ideas.what: If the boundary neighbourhood is 1-equivalent to the open part, then Π_1 of the open moduli space (mapping class group) is the amalgam of codim-1 and codim-2 boundary groupoids
ideas.modern_name: Two-level principle / Grothendieck reconstruction principle for mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, as a claim); proved in versions by Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Boggi; related to Harer's connectivity of the curve complex
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (statement of the principle only)

ideas.what: Flag strata D_{d,d'} of a non-strict normal crossings divisor and compatibility of higher Π̃_i with colimits (margin note)
ideas.modern_name: Stratified/dual-complex (flag) description of normal crossings boundaries; descent along the poset of strata

missed.claim: An explicit topological mechanism for the 'two-level' principle: Π_1 of the structure at infinity is the 2-pushout Π̃_1 ← Π̃_{2,1} → Π̃_2, with codim-3 strata negligible by a local Van Kampen argument, valid for any NC-compactified orbifold. Hence it gives Π_1 of the open part whenever the boundary is 1-equivalent to it. Later proofs (HLS, Boggi) work via curve-complex combinatorics rather than this general geometric formula.
missed.quote: On a Π_1 X^{*∞} ≃ lim→ (Π̃_1 ← Π̃_{2,1} → Π̃_2). En effet, une analyse locale facile (ou du type "Van Kampen") montre qu'on peut ... négliger Θ^{(3)}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck had a general, non-Teichmüller-specific proof strategy for the reconstruction principle. That strategy could apply to other moduli spaces with NC boundary (e.g. toroidal compactifications of Shimura varieties) and to profinite/étale versions relevant to GT.

missed.claim: The margin asks to make explicit how the higher-codimension groupoids Π̃_i (i ≥ 3) are themselves colimits of their flag sub-diagrams (Π̃_{3,2,1} → Π̃_{3,2}, Π̃_{3,1}, …), i.e. a coherent 2-categorical descent description of the whole stratified tower at infinity.
missed.quote: Il faut expliciter aussi comment les Π_i (i≥3) dans le groupoïde lim = Π_1 du voisinage V''*_{Θ,X}, p.ex. comment Π_3 est l'lim du diagramme de groupoïdes Π_{3,2,1} → Π_{3,2}, Π_{3,1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precursor of a functorial 'stratified homotopy type at infinity' (exit-path/stratified groupoids). That framework is now studied in stratified homotopy theory but not linked to Grothendieck's tower.

deep.surprise_reason: The two-level principle itself is announced in the Esquisse and later proved by others. The page adds a clean, general Van Kampen-style pushout formula and an explicit 1-equivalence criterion, a notable unpublished detail of how Grothendieck intended to prove it, but not a genuinely unknown result.
transcription_corrections: In formula (247) the left side reads 'Π_1 X' in the image, but the intended object is Π_1 X* (open part); flag as Grothendieck's slip rather than a transcription error.

Margin: the groupoids are tilde-groupoids Π̃_i, Π̃_{3,2,1}, Π̃_{3,2}, Π̃_{3,1}, Π̃_1, Π̃_{2,1}, Π̃_2; the reading is likely 'comment interviennent les Π̃_i (i≥3) dans le groupoïde lim→ = Π_1 du voisinage V''*_{Θ,X}'.
The crossed-out symbol before X^{*∞} in (246) is V (start of V*), replaced by X^{*∞}.
The word under the right-hand Π̃_1 of (247) appears to read 'généralisation'/'généralités', likely a marginal heading for the crossed-out Corollaire 4.

Crossed-out Corollaire 4: 'Soit d ∈ N, et supposons que pour tout i ≤ d, l'on ait D_i^{*∞} → ...'; then 'Considérons une partie non-multiplicité[?] D'_i d'un D_i qui soit ouverte et fermée, et considérons l'image Θ'^{(i)} ⊂ Θ^{(i)} de D'_i, qui est dans une "strate de codim i"'.
